deye.name: Deye / Sunsynk hybrid inverter (F-codes)
deye.source: https://manualshive.com/en/manual/sunsynk/g01lp1-us-eu/1400613?page=43  |  Deye SUN-3.6/5/6K-SG03LP1-EU instruction manual, chart 7-1 fault information

F01: Panel (PV) wires may be connected the wrong way round. Switch the solar isolator OFF and have a technician check the polarity.
F02: Poor insulation between the solar wiring and earth, often water in connectors. Switch the solar isolator OFF; a technician must test it.
F13: Working mode changed / grid mode changed
Usually clears by itself after the grid or settings change. If it repeats every few minutes, a technician should check the grid and settings.
F18: Often an overload or surge on the AC output. Switch off big appliances and restart once; if it returns, a technician must check it.
F20: Switch off and restart once; if it returns, a technician must check the DC side.
F23: An earthing or insulation problem on PV or AC, often moisture. Do not keep resetting it: a technician must test the earthing.
F24: Solar array insulation to earth is low, often wet MC4 connectors. Switch the solar isolator OFF; a technician must test it.
F26: Restart the system once. With a big difference between L1 and L2 loads (split phase) it can also appear. If it keeps coming back, a technician should check.
F35: Check that the grid supply and the grid breaker are on. If ZESA power is on and it still shows, a technician should check the wiring.
F41: In a parallel setup, one inverter being off can stop the others. Check that every inverter is switched on; if it still shows, a technician should check.
F58: The inverter cannot talk to the battery. Check that the battery is on and the battery comms cable is plugged firmly into the inverter's BMS port, then restart.
F64: The inverter is too hot. Make sure the vents are clear and it is in shade with airflow, reduce the load, and let it cool for 30 minutes.
F08: In a split-phase or three-phase system the backup load N line must be connected to earth. A technician must check the earthing.
F22: Please contact your installer for help.
F29: In a parallel system check the parallel communication cable and the inverter addresses. It can show during start-up and clear by itself once all inverters are on. If it stays, a technician must check.
F34: Check the load on the backup output is within the inverter's range. If the fault still exists, a technician must check it.
F42: AC line low voltage (grid voltage fault)
Check the AC voltage is in the standard range and the grid AC cables are firm and correctly connected. If it cannot go back to normal, a technician must check.
F47: AC over frequency (grid frequency out of range)
Check the grid frequency is within the specification and the AC cables are firm. If it cannot go back to normal, a technician must check.
F48: AC lower frequency (grid frequency out of range)
Check the grid frequency is within the specification and the AC cables are firm. If it cannot go back to normal, a technician must check.
F56: DC busbar voltage too low (battery voltage low)
Check whether the battery voltage is too low. If it is, charge it from solar or the grid. If it cannot go back to normal, a technician must check.
F63: Arc-fault detection (US market). Check the solar panel cable connections; a technician must clear the fault.

voltronic.name: Axpert / Voltronic family: Axpert, Mecer, Kodak, Conversol, MPP Solar, Must, Voltacon and similar (numbered faults)

01: Check that the vents are clear and the fan is not blocked; if the fan is stuck a technician must replace it.
02: Too hot: improve ventilation or shade, reduce the load, let it cool. If it happens in a cool place, a technician must check.
03: Switch off and have a technician check the battery settings, the number of batteries and the charger.
04: The battery is flat. Reduce loads and let it recharge; if the battery is old or will not hold charge, a technician must test it.
05: Output short circuit or over temperature
Switch off the AC output and unplug all appliances; a short circuit in a socket or appliance is likely. Restart once, then add appliances one by one.
06: Output voltage abnormal (below 190 V or above 260 V)
Reduce the load and restart once. If it repeats with no load, a technician must check it.
07: Too much load for too long. Switch off the heavy appliances (geyser, stove, pump, heater) and restart.
08: An internal fault, often seen with some models when charging from the grid. Switch off and call a technician: do not keep restarting.
09: Internal fault. Switch off and call a technician.
51: Switch off heavy loads and restart once; if it returns, a technician must check.
52: Internal fault. Switch off and call a technician.
53: Internal fault. Switch off and call a technician.
55: Over DC voltage in AC output
Internal fault. Switch off and call a technician.
56: Switch everything off and check that the battery breaker/fuse is ON and the battery cables are tight (look only; do not open the unit). If fine, a technician must check.
57: Internal fault. Switch off and call a technician.
58: Reduce the load and restart once. If it repeats with no load, a technician must check it.
80: Check the parallel/communication cables between units are seated firmly.
81: Check the parallel/communication cables between units are seated firmly.

victron.name: Victron MultiPlus / Quattro (VE.Bus errors and LEDs)

1: A device in the system has switched off (usually low battery, overload or high temperature)
Look at the LEDs on the unit that is off: they tell you which alarm it was. Reduce the load, charge the battery, or cool it down.
3: Often follows error 1: fix the cause of error 1 first, then check the network cables between units.
7: External device connected but no Assistant set up for it
A technician must configure the unit.
8: A technician must check the earthing and the unit.
2: New and old type MK2 protocol mixed in the system
This should never happen. A technician must check it. Please don't keep resetting it.
4: No other device found (parallel, split or three-phase set-up)
It can show briefly while the system restarts. If it stays, the network cables between the units are the likely cause: a technician should check them.
5: Usually the AC wiring of one unit is not connected properly. Switch off and have a technician check the AC wiring.
6: The firmware and configuration need updating. A technician must check it. Please don't keep resetting it.
10: Often only shows while restarting and is not a real fault; the real cause is usually error 1 or a blown DC fuse. If it stays, a technician should check.
11: Relay test fault (installation error or relay failure)
The wiring, earthing or a relay may be at fault. A technician must check it. Please don't keep resetting it.
12: Configuration mismatch between the unit's two processors (MultiPlus-II models)
The settings must be re-sent by a technician.
14: Most likely a short in the communication cables, rarely a failed board. A technician must check it. Please don't keep resetting it.
15: VE.Bus combination error (products, firmware or commands do not match)
Usually fixed by a firmware update. A technician must check it. Please don't keep resetting it.
16: A firmware update is needed. The system stays off until restarted. A technician must check it. Please don't keep resetting it.
17: Can show briefly while settings are being written. If it stays, a communication cable or a blown DC fuse is the usual cause: a technician should check.
18: AC overvoltage on the output of a slave unit while it is switched off
AC wires may be swapped. Switch off and have a technician check.
19: A slave unit has no AC input
AC input must be connected to every unit in the set, or the 'Switch as Group' setting changed by a technician.
20: Configuration mismatch (extended options are not allowed with a grid code)
The configuration must be corrected by a technician.
22: This device cannot work as a slave (obsolete model)
The unit has to be replaced: ask a technician.
24: Current was detected through the back-feed relay when it should be open. A technician must check the settings and relay.
25: Incompatible VE.Bus configuration (mixed firmware or compatibility IDs)
All units need matching firmware. A technician must check it. Please don't keep resetting it.
26: This should not occur. Switch everything off and on once; if it returns, call a technician.
30: Interference on the VE.Bus network cabling ('ghost' error)
Usually caused by the communication cables. A technician should check the cabling.
31: Interference on the VE.Bus network cabling ('ghost' error)
Usually caused by the communication cables. A technician should check the cabling.
128: Relay test failed, so the unit cannot connect to the grid (Quattro-II with a grid code)
A technician must check it. Please don't keep resetting it.

goodwe.name: GoodWe ES / EM hybrid inverter (error messages shown in the PV Master / SolarGo app)
goodwe.source: https://portal.segensolar.co.za/reseller/docs/ES USER MANUAL.pdf (section 4.1, Error message and troubleshootings)

Utility Loss: Check that grid power is on and the AC breaker is on, and that the AC cables are tight. If all looks fine, switch the AC breaker off and on again after 5 minutes.
VAC Failure: Grid voltage outside the permitted range
Often caused by an unstable grid. If it keeps happening, a technician should check the AC voltage and the inverter's safety-country setting.
FAC Failure: Grid frequency outside the permitted range
If it only appears a few times and clears, it is the grid. If it keeps happening, a technician should check the safety-country setting.
PV Over Voltage: A technician must check the number of panels in each string against the inverter's limit.
Over Temperature: Improve ventilation or shade and reduce the load. Switch it off for 15 minutes, then start it again. If it returns, a technician must check.
Isolation Failure: Solar string insulation to earth too low
Often water in connectors, damaged DC cable or ageing panels. A technician must test it.
Ground I Failure: Neutral and earth on the AC side may not be connected well. A technician must check it. If it only happens early morning or on rainy days and clears, it can be humidity.
Relay Check Failure: Neutral and earth may be poorly connected, or it was a one-off. Restart once; if it returns a technician must check.
DC Injection High: Too much DC in the AC output
Restart the inverter once. If it comes back, contact a technician.
EEPROM R/W Failure: Restart the inverter once. If it comes back, contact a technician.
SPI Failure: Restart the inverter once. If it comes back, contact a technician.
DC Bus High: Restart the inverter once. If it comes back, contact a technician.
Back-Up Over Load: Switch off some appliances on the back-up output so the total load is below the back-up rating.
